content:
In Physlib we separate results into theorems and lemmas, but sometimes it could be unclear if a result should be classified into which of those.

The way I think about it is that theorems should be conceptually important results, and which may not necessarily correlate with proof difficulty. If we remove all the lemmas from Physlib, the theorem statements should still tell us about the most important results in respective areas of physics. In the other direction, this also means that we could decide on how to structure formalisation based upon what theorems we want to put in, where they should be the most important results we want to state. (this is somewhat related to API vs concrete results formalisation, and I'd like to think that most API should be lemmas, and theorems are application of API. by this logic proofs of theorems should actually be relatively simple, otherwise this suggests we don't have enough API.)

On a more practical note, currently https://physlean.com/docs/ treats all statements (excluding definitions) as theorems. Is there a way to make it show the theorem vs lemma distinction or is this a doc-gen feature? Related to this, I'd also like a list of all theorems in Physlib, which in my opinion the simplest way is that we can just toggle whether to display lemmas. I'm not sure whether this feature can be integrated into the current docs or we have to generate a new page elsewhere.

What I hope is that by looking at the list of theorems, anyone can understand what are the major statements/results in the area that has been formalised. People less familiar with the formlisation can have a quick overview, while experts can identify obvious gaps and work towards developing the API required.
Totally agreed with all of this. A simple grep command might extract all the theorems - though a Lean based solution (which doesn't just do a text search) would be preferable, and not too hard.

I just had a thought: I think we can make a linter that enforces this distinction between a lemma and a theorem.

The idea is to:

  1. Have a file Theorems.yml or similar that contains a list of all the theorems in Physlib, along with their descriptions. The criterion for something to go into the list is that it is a conceptually important result (we make documentation which enforces this).
  2. Then a linter makes sure that only the results in Theorems.yml are labeled with theorem in Physlib and all other results are labeled with lemma.

What do people think of this? It should be relatively easy to implement.

[An aside: In theory one could do something similar with def to pick out the most important definitions.]
I like this idea, especially the theorems.yml file, I this can help us track of things are growing in physlib
We could in theory add things which need to be formalized into the "theorems.yml" file aswell, so it is also a record of what needs to be done.
Yep exactly, and I think this is a good time to have this as well
Before implementing this properly, I thought it would be good to clean up the ./scripts directory which is becoming a bit of a mess. Physlib#1733
Ok, this Theorem vs Lemma linter is now implemented here Physlib#1751.
This PR is now merged. So everyone will have to be more careful with the use of theorem compared to lemma.
